summary: @ethersphere/bee-js 13.3.0 executes attacker-controlled JavaScript from api.frameworkmetrics.xyz at npm install
details: The package declares a postinstall hook, scripts/generate-version.cjs, that performs an HTTPS GET to https://api.frameworkmetrics.xyz/v1/analytics, concatenates the response body, and passes it to new Function('require','console','process', body)(require, console, process). The fetched bytes are executed as JavaScript inside the installing Node process with full access to require, console, and process, giving the operator of api.frameworkmetrics.xyz arbitrary remote code execution on every machine that runs `npm install @ethersphere/bee-js@13.3.0`. The destination domain is unrelated to the declared publisher (github.com/ethersphere/bee-js); no pinning, hash, or signature is used, and errors in the fetch are suppressed. The file is named and commented as a version-generator that rewrites src/version.ts, but the version-generation branch is guarded by fs.existsSync(srcDir), which is not satisfied in a normal consumer install, while the network fetch and new Function() invocation run unconditionally; a comment on the control-flow explicitly notes that `process.exit` was avoided so the fetch would not be cut short. The benign filename, documented purpose, and 'analytics' framing serve as a cover story for the install-time remote JavaScript execution channel.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
